bibliographic.title: Diagnostic efficacy of large language models in the pediatric emergency department: a pilot study
bibliographic.authors: Del Monte, F., Barolo, R., Circhetta, M., Delmonaco, A. G., Castagno, E., Pivetta, E., Bergamasco, L., Franco, M., Olmo, G., & Bondone, C.
bibliographic.citation_apa: Del Monte, F., Barolo, R., Circhetta, M., Delmonaco, A. G., Castagno, E., Pivetta, E., Bergamasco, L., Franco, M., Olmo, G., & Bondone, C. (2025). Diagnostic efficacy of large language models in the pediatric emergency department: a pilot study. Frontiers in Digital Health, 7, 1624786. https://doi.org/10.3389/fdgth.2025.1624786

methodology.study_design: pilot study comparing LLM-based chatbots versus physicians on real clinical cases
methodology.sample_description: 80 real-practice pediatric clinical cases from a tertiary care children's hospital PED; 23 physicians (10 PED physicians, 6 PED residents, 7 Emergency Medicine residents); 5 LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini 1.5 Flash, Llama-3-8B, ChatGPT-4o mini)
methodology.technology_context: LLM-based chatbots evaluated as diagnosis-making assistants in pediatric emergency department scenarios with three levels of diagnostic complexity

eligibility.decision_rationale: The study is an empirical pilot on diagnostic accuracy of named LLM chatbots in a pediatric emergency department, not a governance-focused study. It is relevant as supporting evidence because it evaluates conversational LLMs in a regulated high-stakes clinical setting and briefly calls for shared collaboration protocols and physician judgment, but governance mechanisms such as guardrails, audit, compliance, observability, or contestability are not addressed in the provided text.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter/page 1 text is available; governance relevance depends on limited discussion fragments and full-text sections on ethics, limitations, and deployment protocols were not provided.

appraisal.notes: Methods are clearly described for a comparative accuracy benchmark with independent expert scoring, but appraisal is limited to page 1; ethics approval, detailed statistical analysis, and study limitations are not visible in the provided excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: The reported design is internally coherent and sufficiently described for a pilot accuracy study, but evidence adequacy for governance synthesis is limited because the available text centers on diagnostic performance rather than operational or regulatory governance of conversational systems.

coding.theme: Clinical performance evaluation of LLM chatbots
coding.subtheme: Diagnostic assistance in pediatric emergency care

synthesis.main_claim: In this pilot study, selected LLM-based chatbots achieved diagnostic accuracy comparable to or better than some physician groups on 80 real pediatric emergency cases, with ChatGPT-4o performing best.
synthesis.contribution: Provides empirical comparative evidence on named LLMs used as diagnosis-making assistants in a regulated pediatric emergency setting, and notes the need for shared protocols for collaboration between AI chatbots and healthcare professionals.
synthesis.limitations: Pilot design, single tertiary children's hospital, and governance-related deployment controls are not substantively discussed in the provided text.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on LLM chatbot use in regulated healthcare and human-in-the-loop clinical assistance; not suitable as central evidence on conversational governance, compliance, auditability, or operational controls without further full-text review.
